Security Findings.title: Exposed network service: http
Security Findings.description: Enumeration reported this service as open from the scan vantage point. The results do not establish whether it is necessary or appropriately restricted.
Security Findings.attack_scenario: An authorized tester could verify that the service is intended to be reachable from this network segment and review its access controls.
Security Findings.impact: An exposed service increases the reachable network surface; impact depends on its purpose, configuration, and access controls.
Security Findings.remediation: Confirm the service is required, restrict it to trusted sources, and disable it if it is not needed.
evidence: Enumeration reported TCP port 80 as open.
references: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, Control 4: Secure Configuration of Enterprise Assets and Software

Security Findings.title: Cleartext-capable protocol exposed
Security Findings.description: The observed HTTP service may transmit data or credentials without transport encryption. Enumeration did not verify application-level settings.
Security Findings.attack_scenario: An authorized tester could verify with non-sensitive test traffic whether the service negotiates encryption and protects communications on this path.
Security Findings.impact: Where encryption is absent, network observers may be able to read or alter traffic in transit, depending on protocol and network position.
Security Findings.remediation: Prefer an encrypted alternative or enforce secure transport, restrict access, and avoid sending credentials or sensitive data in cleartext.
evidence: Enumeration reported TCP port 80 as open.
references: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SC-8: Transmission Confidentiality and Integrity

Security Findings.title: Web service exposed
Security Findings.description: Enumeration indicates a web endpoint. This does not establish an application vulnerability or whether broader network access is intended.
Security Findings.attack_scenario: An authorized tester could review the endpoint's intended audience, authentication boundaries, transport security, and application configuration.
Security Findings.impact: The endpoint adds an application surface reachable from the assessed network; impact depends on application design and access controls.
Security Findings.remediation: Limit access to intended users and networks, use HTTPS for sensitive traffic, and maintain the web server and application.

Security Findings.title: Web response omitted security headers
Security Findings.description: The observed HEAD response did not include one or more common browser security headers. This single response does not establish behavior on every path or application page.
Security Findings.attack_scenario: An authorized reviewer could check whether the application's browser-facing routes need these headers and confirm the behavior across representative pages.
Security Findings.impact: Depending on application behavior, missing browser security headers may reduce defense-in-depth against content and framing risks.
Security Findings.remediation: Configure applicable headers at the web server or application layer and verify them on representative responses.
evidence: The HEAD response did not include: content-security-policy, x-content-type-options, x-frame-options, referrer-policy, permissions-policy.
Observed HEAD response omitted these headers: content-security-policy, x-content-type-options, x-frame-options, referrer-policy, permissions-policy.
references: OWASP Secure Headers Project
OWASP Application Security Verification Standard (ASVS)

Security Findings.title: TLS certificate validation failed
Security Findings.description: The standard TLS client rejected the peer certificate. This assessment records the validation result but does not infer why it failed beyond the evidence.
Security Findings.attack_scenario: An authorized tester could verify the certificate chain, validity period, and service name against the intended endpoint configuration.
Security Findings.impact: Clients may be unable to verify the endpoint identity, or users may be prompted to bypass certificate warnings.
Security Findings.remediation: Install a certificate from an appropriate trust chain, ensure its names match the intended endpoint, and renew it before expiry.
